snippet.title: Did People Really Think Birds Flew to the Moon?
snippet.description:
In the 17th century, Charles Morton suggested that swallows and storks wintered on the Moon. On May 21, 1822, a white stork shot near Klütz carried an 80-centimeter arrow from Central Africa in its neck, becoming the first physical evidence of long-distance migration among European birds.

requested.title: The Scholar Who Thought Birds Spent Winter on the Moon
requested.description:
In the 17th century, English scholar Charles Morton proposed that swallows and storks spent the winter on the Moon. More than a century later, a remarkable stork offered a different clue.

Shot near Klütz, Germany, in 1822, the bird carried an arrow from Central Africa in its neck. It had crossed a great distance, providing physical evidence of long-distance bird migration. The specimen is preserved at the University of Rostock.
